text:
Marathon Petroleum shares fell nearly 1.5% over the past two weeks, with steep declines this week (down 11% since November 13th). The most direct driver is a shift in market sentiment: energy analysts are signaling that the exceptional profit run refiners have enjoyed is ending, and investors are rotating out of refinery stocks. Oil prices themselves remain reasonably firm—US crude at $89.53 and global at $92.94—and refineries are running at a healthy 95.7% capacity, so the fundamentals haven't collapsed; rather, the market is repricing what it's willing to pay for refiner earnings going forward.

The broader context matters here: geopolitical tension in the Middle East (Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries, Iranian drone operations) would normally support refiner stocks by keeping oil prices elevated, but that tailwind isn't enough to offset the narrative shift. The failed climate talks at COP31 might have been expected to help fossil fuel traders, yet the opposite is playing out—the investment community appears to be ahead of that curve, already moving capital away from the energy trade that made refiners such strong performers.
